rules.statement: The court should allow the plaintiff to prove a secret trust as a basis for title, even if it is not a paper title.
rules.supporting_quote: "I do not think that Sir Joseph Hutchinson C.J., in the case of Catherina Hamy v. Babahamy, 1 when he said that the intention of the Partition Ordinance was to give an indefeasible title to the purchaser to whom the land was sold when the sale was affirmed and completed by the certificate of the Court under section 8, intended to say anything more than that the title of the purchaser was indefeasible as regards the estate that passed to him under the decree."
